perspective:
**Angela Hwang’s accessible perspective:**

- I am Angela Hwang, a hairdresser with a doctorate. Kevin Flores is my close friend since high school; we confide in each other. I know he works in construction.
- I noticed Kevin seemed unhappy with his construction job, so I invited him to coffee. He told me he was “alright, just the usual grind,” then admitted he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was just going through the motions.
- I asked if he had thought about a different job or career. He said he had, but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed. I offered to figure it out together and look into options. He agreed and thanked me.
- I believed Kevin was considering a career change, and I felt supportive and hopeful. I found job openings and a career counseling service and shared them with him. He thanked me and said he was interested in something more creative, maybe design or architecture. I encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would and that my support meant a lot.
- I believed Kevin was hesitant, and I felt frustrated and worried. I arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. He said I didn’t have to, appreciated it, but was not sure he was ready. I told him sometimes people need a push and the coach could help him make a plan and gain confidence. He agreed to give it a shot. I promised to support him.
- I believed Kevin was making progress. I checked in. He told me the career coach had been helpful, he had started online courses in design, and he felt more confident. I said I was proud of him and offered more help. He said knowing I was there was enough and he would tell me if he needed anything. I said I would always be there for him.
- I believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career, and I felt happy and satisfied. I organized a small celebration party and told him. He thanked me, said he was grateful, and said he couldn’t have done it without me. I said he did the hard work and I was glad I could support him. We celebrated.

**Kevin explicitly told Angela:** he was unhappy/stuck/unfulfilled at work; he had thought about change but didn’t know where to start; he was interested in creative work such as design or architecture; the career coach helped; he started online design courses and felt more confident; he appreciated her support and could not have done it without her.

**Angela’s own actions:** inviting Kevin to coffee, asking about his feelings, suggesting career options, researching and sharing job/career resources, arranging a career-coach meeting, checking in regularly, offering ongoing help, and organizing a celebration party.

**Not available to Angela:** Kevin’s private or unspoken thoughts, hidden events she did not observe, and narrator-only facts beyond what Kevin told her and what she experienced or believed.
